headline: War on the Rocks warned that frontier AI is testing the limits of human oversight in security and defense, as former Army Secretary Dan Driscoll joined OpenAI and the UN published an FAQ for its Bridgetown Special Summit on AI Safety.

points.text: War on the Rocks argued that frontier AI systems are beginning to test the limits of human oversight, while the companies developing them retain considerable power to define the risks and terms of their own scrutiny, especially in security and defense.
Former US Army Secretary Dan Driscoll is joining OpenAI, saying he wants to help the United States and its allies put the technology to work responsibly for the people who keep them safe.
At the AUSA 2026 conference, Breaking Defense examined the US Army's push into autonomous warfare and drone innovation alongside acquisition reform.
The UN Tech Envoy published an FAQ for the Bridgetown Special Summit on AI Safety, clarifying that it will not create global AI rules or replace national decision-making.
MIT Technology Review described 'reverse game theory,' a new approach to keeping AI agents in check by designing systems that incentivize models to stick to the rules.
